_help: Volunteer stories for stories.html, shown in this order: the volunteer's photo, then their words in a yellow card. Edit on GitHub (pencil icon), then commit: the site republishes itself. One story = one { } block, separated by commas. VOLUNTEERS ONLY: never a kid's story, name, age or photo here. Every real story needs the volunteer's written OK: put the month you got it in "consent" (like "2026-11"). "photo" is optional: a portrait photo of the volunteer, the shape of a normal phone photo (3:4, 900 x 1200, under 200 KB, webp, no kids in it) in images/stories/; without one the page shows 'Photo coming soon'. "rating" (1 to 5 stars) is optional. While any story has "placeholder": true, the page stays out of search results: replace the placeholder blocks as real stories come in.

_example.name: First name, or first name + initial
_example.quote:
What a class is like, a moment they remember, why they keep coming back. 40 to 100 words works best. A line break (
) starts a new paragraph.

stories.name: Manmohan
stories.quote:
I began volunteering because I have a love for teaching and enjoy spending time with kids. However, I never anticipated the level of happiness and purpose this would add to my own life. I know that I have impacted the children’s lives here but little do they know how much of an impact they have on my life.
This experience has surprised me in many ways and has shown me a greater appreciation for the things I have in life and for the many little things that we often take for granted. It has truly been a humbling and loving experience for me this far.

stories.name: Volunteer name
stories.quote: When I first met my student, he seemed like a kid who was constantly scanning his surroundings, observing everything before deciding to let loose. But as the classes went by, I watched him gradually come out of his shell, become more comfortable, and start expressing himself. My mission has always been bigger than just teaching him English. I want him to question things, challenge assumptions, think critically, and develop that beautiful scientific mindset. After all, the world doesn't need more people who blindly accept things; it needs people who ask WHY! Every class has been another opportunity to spark some curiosity, trigger a few brain cells, and unleash a little intellectual dynamite. I'm proud of how far he's come, and believe me, he's got a whole lot of potential waiting to EXPLODE!

stories.name: Volunteer name
stories.quote: I remember the day I met my student, he was quiet and shy, nothing but a few “yes akkas”. I worried initially that he wasn’t comprehending the subject matter, but soon enough I understood his process. He prefers one-on-one teaching, while other students would utilise breaks to go outside and play, he requested that I go through the material again with him so he could learn at a pace that suited him. Despite having limited classes, he never used that as an excuse to underperform. His growth was incredible and so heartwarming to witness. I’m happy to say that he has since moved up a level and continues to work hard. I am beyond proud to have been his teacher.
